images.caption: FORT LIBERTY, N.C. – Completed in April 2012, the new Irwin Intermediate School at Fort Liberty opened just in time for the 2012-2013 school year. Construction on the $14.9 million, 112,025-square-foot facility began in 2010 and was managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Savannah District. The new school replaces the original Irwin building built in 1962. The school was formally dedicated with an opening ceremony on Sept. 27, 2012. It was named in memory of Lt. Gen. Stafford Leroy Irwin, who served as the post commander from 1946 to 1948. Located off of Normandy Drive, near Butler and Murray elementary schools, the new Irwin School serves 725 students in grades two through five. Amenities include art, music, and general purpose classrooms, computer labs, a playground, gymnasium, and multipurpose rooms with a stage and kitchen. Within the past few years, the Savannah District has completed more than $100 million in family support projects at Fort Liberty, including schools and child development centers. Between 2013 and 2020, another $90 million is budgeted for continued school development on Fort Liberty. USACE photo by Tracy Robillard, Sept. 12, 2012.

images.caption: The Guest House Museum located at 343 North Main Street, en:Fort Bragg, California is operated by the Fort Bragg — Mendocino Coast Historical Society. The Guest House was named a California Point of Historical Interest #P673 in 1986 by the Native Daughters of the Golden West Fort Bragg Parlor 210. The base of clock reads "in memory of Ethel Wikstom Lynn 1895 - 1993".
